chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from 'Abbad ibn Suhayb from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man whom the Imam stopped for al-li'an (conjugal imprecation), and he gave two testimonies, then hesitated/refrained from himself before finishing, or he lied about himself from the li'an. He said: 'He is flogged with the hadd punishment and he is not separated from his wife.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on li'an if the husband hesitates or lies before completing the oath?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq clarifies that if a husband in the *li'an* process hesitates or contradicts himself before completion, he is subjected to the *hadd* punishment of flogging but the marital bond remains intact (*la yufarraq*). This ruling highlights the Shia juristic view that an incomplete *li'an* does not trigger the automatic triple divorce associated with its full completion, preserving the family unit while imposing disciplinary penalty on the accuser.
